title: Conflicts: last write wins, and what it silently throws away

videos.script:
Two devices, one session, no network. {{phone}} On the train, Ana changes her guitar session to thirty minutes. {{tablet}} At home, a quarter of an hour later, she ticks the same session done on her tablet.

Both devices save. Both tell her it worked. {{syncs}} Later, each one finds a network and sends its copy.

That is a conflict. Nothing crashes, and nothing turns red. The server simply has two versions of one row, and it keeps one of them.

The rule most apps start with is last write wins. {{rule}} Keep the newest stamp, drop the other row whole. Today you run it, and watch one of Ana's edits disappear without a word.

Then you ask whose clock says which write was last. {{clock}} The phone's, which can be two hours wrong. Or the server's, which only knows who synced last.

And you finish by sorting the data. {{fields}} For a setting, the rule is right. For a counter, it is a bug.
